report:
Fresh final followup review of implementation_coverage. Saved/read prior report and inputs, started fresh, recaptured all six dependencies and compared every fragment. Claim, both test bodies and all evidence/correspondence/check/helper captures are unchanged. The sole spec.rs delta is the implementation_references association comment on the separate unknown-reference validator; coverage behavior is unchanged.

The full claim requires every anchor to have an explicit Rust implementation entry, errors for missing entries, no substitution by tests or modeled-item correspondence, and placeholder entries counted with their explicit status. The sole ordinary implementation validate_implementations checks each anchor against only the implementations map and requires a nonempty vector. Missing and empty vectors produce a diagnostic at the defining source location. Test and item maps cannot satisfy this predicate. The captured main check invokes it independently from test validation; correspondence invokes the dedicated evidence indexer into the separate implementation map. Captured evidence construction preserves module-derived Ordinary/Todo/NotApplicable status, rationale and source metadata. Coverage accepts any nonempty entry vector without relabeling placeholders; conflicting placeholder ancestry produces its own error. The new marker does not affect any path.

The complete ordinary test tests_and_model_correspondence_do_not_replace_explicit_implementation_entries constructs a definition and real indexed Rust with both sage::item and sage::test but no implementation comment. It requires successful test validation, exactly one implementation diagnostic and the missing-Rust-implementation message. This directly exercises independence even when both other evidence types exist. Its captured source helper forwards actual text into SpecSource.

The sole TODO independent_implementation_coverage remains empty and explicit about the broader missing-entry/placeholder-status matrix. The ordinary test covers the combined negative scenario; separate cases and direct positive ordinary/TODO/N/A acceptance/status assertions remain deferred. Completing that verification requires distinct inventory fixtures and explicit acceptance/status assertions. Current source supports the predicate and retained statuses, but the TODO is not counted as behavioral proof or silently retired. No N/A evidence entry exists for this anchor.

The actual marker-only change was checked against the complete prior assessment, and all other relied-on inputs were verified unchanged. Full claim aspects remain implemented with the stated visible test deferral. No source edits, build or behavior tests occurred in this review; fresh start/read/record and source inspection only. No requested edits.
